question: In all of the following enzyme deficiencies, hyperammonemia is a common feature, EXCEPT:

analysis: In the context of urea cycle disorders, hyperammonemia is a common feature of several enzyme deficiencies. Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency (option opa), Carbamoyl Phosphate synthetase (CPS-I) deficiency (option opb), and Ornithine transcarbamoylase (OTC) deficiency (option opc) all lead to significant disruptions in the urea cycle, resulting in the accumulation of ammonia in the bloodstream. In contrast, Ornithine amino transferase deficiency (option opd) is less directly associated with hyperammonemia, as it primarily affects the transamination of ornithine and does not lead to the same level of ammonia accumulation as the other deficiencies. Therefore, the exception among the listed enzyme deficiencies that commonly feature hyperammonemia is Ornithine amino transferase deficiency. This conclusion is supported by the consensus in biochemical and metabolic literature regarding the pathways involved in these enzyme deficiencies.
